newsitem.title: USA: Union presses Mellon for help in WHX strike.
newsitem.headline: Union presses Mellon for help in WHX strike.

text.p: Leaders of the United Steelworkers of America on Monday said the union would launch actions across Pennsylvania aimed at persuading Mellon Bank Corp to intervene in a nine-month-old strike against WHX Corp .

At a news conference, union president George Becker said Mellon is a major WHX shareholder and should therefore urge the steelmaker's chairman, Ron LaBow, to return to the bargaining table to settle the dispute with the union.

He said Mellon has rebuffed the union's requests for the company to intervene in the dispute. "(WHX's major shareholders) have sat by, watching silently as the value of their stock plummeted, as the future of the steel company was placed in jeopardy," Becker said.
Earlier Monday, Mellon said in a statement that the company and its subsidiaries do not own and have not owned shares in WHX, and cannot intervene in the dispute.
"All of the shares held by Mellon or its subsidiaries in WHX are held in a fiduciary capacity on behalf of clients," the company said.
Some 4,500 steelworkers have been on strike against WHX since October 1, when their contract expired and negotiations failed to produce a new agreement.
The strike has idled eight steel plants in Pennsylvania, Ohio and West Virginia.

The dispute centers around pensions. Union members are demanding the company establish a defined benefit plan, while the company has maintained it cannot afford such a plan and instead has offered to enhance its existing defined contribution plan.
Negotiations -- held periodically since the strike began -- have broken off, with the two sides appearing to be no closer to an agreement.

Becker said the actions that the union will take against Mellon include asking its more than 150,000 active members and retirees across Pennsylvania to withdraw their funds from the bank, which is based in Pittsburgh.
Becker also said the union would launch a "major campaign" to tell the public about the issues surrounding the strike and "Mellon's responsibility to help settle the dispute."
Becker said he wrote to Frank Cahouet, Mellon's chairman, asking him to use the bank's influence with LaBow.
"The bank's response has been, in effect, to wash its hands of the matter," he said. "This refusal to get involved is unacceptable."
